transcript.text: How is everybody doing? Welcome back to another Dragon Wilds video. With the recent changes that accompanied the 1.0.1
update, the best in-class jewelry in Dragon Wilds has changed drastically. Now, depending on what you're using, you
might actually be losing out on a pretty significant amount of damage. The Amulet of Glory, which has been one of the
strongest pieces of jewelry for a very long time, has received a substantial nerf. What's interesting is that this
change has pushed some older jewelry back into the spotlight, specifically the unholy symbol and the solve amulet.
Now, this update also introduce separate slots for rings as well as amulets. And this is important because there is
currently a very interesting combination that allows us to stack two powerful damage bonuses together. And I'm going
to be straightforward with you guys. I think that this is going to get changed. But in this video, I'm going to break
down exactly what's changed, which jewelry is now worth using, what you should be equipping depending on your
combat style and the enemies you're fighting. Starting with the Amulet of Glory. Now, like I said, this has been
one of the most valuable pieces of jewelry because it provides bonuses across all three combat styles while
also giving you a small but beneficial defensive benefit. For this update, the glory provided a flat 25% damage
increase for melee and magic alongside a 25% critical damage bonus for range combat. Well, with the 1.0.1 update,
those numbers have been reduced quite substantially. Melee damage has dropped from 25% to 12.5% and magic damage has
also dropped from 25% to 12.5%. Now, rang's critical damage bonuses have been reduced from 25% to 15%. So, we're
looking at the melee and magic bonuses being cut directly in half. While range has also taken a noticeable reduction.
Now, that doesn't mean the amulet of glory is suddenly now a bad piece of equipment to use. It's still extremely
useful because it gives you bonuses across multiple combat styles, and you don't have to constantly be switching
jewelry depending on the weapon you're using, and still makes it very versatile. When you're looking
specifically at maximizing damage, there are now some better options that are more versatile. And this is exactly how
I want Dragon Wilds to go. I want them to diversify the gear sets, the armor pieces, the jewelry pieces, so we can
have better diversity in build crafting in this game. Now, the first piece of jewelry I want to highlight is the
unholy symbol. This is a piece of gear that was very good when it first released, but it has since been
overlooked previously because the amulet of glory was simply providing a larger damage increase. But after these
changes, the unholy symbol has become one of the strongest generalpurpose damage accessories in the game. The
unholy symbol provides a flat 15% damage increase across all three combat styles. That means whether you're using melee
weapons, magic, or range weapons, especially with the range changes recently, you're receiving the same
damage bonus, which is great. Now, compare this to the Amulet of Glory, which now provides a 12.5% for melee and
magic. The unholy symbol comes out ahead for both of those styles. For range combat, the unholy symbol also has a
major advantage in consistency because it's increasing your regular base damage rather than only boosting critical
damage. Now, however, there is a trade-off. The unholy symbol reduces your maximum health while equipped.
Previously, this was a flat reduction of 15 health, but now with the sanguin urns and getting your health up to 310 max,
it seems that the amulet now works off a percentage base reduction of approximately 15%. So, whenever you do
find this weapon and how many Sanguin earns you're going to get, it's going to be 15% of your base health rather than
15 health across the board. So, keep that in mind. Now, that is a pretty significant difference, especially when
you're working with higher health totals. The higher the health, the more health is going to be decreased because
of that 15%. To give you guys a good example, the current highest health you can get in the game is 310. And when
wearing the unholy symbol, it will reduce your health to 264 after equipping it. So, while the unholy
symbol is still an excellent choice for dealing damage, you're potentially sacrificing a fairly significant amount
of survivability to get that increase. Now, for players who are comfortable avoiding damage, getting out of harm's
way, and don't easily get hit often, especially those using range weapons or magic, that trade-off may be worthwhile
for you. But if you're fighting difficult enemies or taking a lot of hits, it's something you'll want to
consider later on down the line if you want to be using this gear piece. Now, the next piece of jewelry I want to go
over, and this one's going to be pretty interesting. This is a solve amulet. Now, this is mainly important for
players who are spending time in Fel Hollow, but even the raid has undead enemies as well, so it can work there
because a solve amulet provides a 17% damage increase against undead enemies, and that applies across all combat
styles. Now, this makes it an extremely strong choice for fighting undead because you're getting a larger damage
bonus than the unholy symbols, 15% without taking the health penalty associated with that item. The
limitation is that the solve amulet only provides this bonus against undead enemies, like I said. But if you're
farming zers, you're farming enemies in fell hollow, or you're taking on undead enemies in other areas of the map like
the raid doubt unreach, so on and so forth, this piece of gear now outclasses the unholy symbol. Now, with all of
this, this is where things get particularly interesting, and I mentioned it at the beginning of the
video. One of the changes introduced with the 1.0.1 update is that rings and amulets finally have separate equipment
slots. Previously, we had to make a decision about which jewelry item we wanted to equipped. With these dedicated
slots, we can now use a ring and an amulet at the same time. This opens up more opportunities to combine different
bonuses, whether that's additional damage, defensive effects, or utility like XP bonuses. And that's mainly how
I'm going to be using it on fresh characters, is using XP rings. And you guys will understand why in a minute
here. Currently, there is a strange interaction with the unholy symbol. Despite the item's description
identifying it as a necklace, the game currently allows it to occupy the ring slot. Because of this, it's possible to
equip both the unholy symbol and the amulet of glory simultaneously. Now, this is insane because both items
provide damage bonuses. These bonuses appear to be additive rather than multiplicative. So, for melee and magic,
the unholy symbols 15% damage increase and the amulet of glory's 12.5% damage increase would give you a combined bonus
of 27.5%. For range combat, you would receive the unholy symbols flat 15% damage increase
alongside the glory's separate 15% critical damage bonus. I do want to emphasize again, guys, this is most
likely an unintended interaction. The unholy symbol is described as a necklace, so being able to be in the
ring slot most likely is something that's going to get corrected in a very quick future update. But if the
interaction is still working when you're watching this video and just in general before they fix this, if they fix it,
they may not, is definitely something I want you guys to know about. So, with all of these changes, what should you
actually be using? In my opinion, for general combat, if your goal is dealing as much damage as possible, the unholy
symbol is now one of the strongest options available. It's 15% damage increase applies across every combat
style, and you don't have to rely on critical hits to benefit from it. If you're using melee or magic and you want
a little more survivability, the amulet of glory remains a good alternative. You're giving up a small amount of
offensive damage compared to the unholy symbol, but you're also avoiding its health penalty while retaining the
glory's defensive bonuses. Now, for players who are working through fell hollow or specifically farming undead
enemies in that region or endowed unreach or the raid, the solve amulet is the obvious option to have available.
17% increase against undead makes it incredibly useful throughout those encounters and regions. Now, finally, if
the unholy symbol and amulet of glory can still be equipped together, that combination is particularly powerful for
general combat across the board. Now, you would have two separate damage bonuses working together with a 27.5
increase for melee and magic. While range benefits from both a flat damage increase and additional critical damage,
again, just keep in mind that this interaction may not be permanent. I honestly don't think it's going to be.
So, use it while you can. And if it does stay, that's going to be insane and fantastic. Ultimately, update 1.0.1 has
made jewelry a much more interesting part of our equipment setup, class building, and the way we want to build
our character. The Amulet of Glory is no longer the automatic choice for every situation in my opinion. And that's open
the door for equipment like the unholy symbol, the solve, and other pieces of gear that are going to be viable in the
future, as well as new pieces of gear that they're going to introduce. And again, the unholy symbol is excellent
general damage option. The solve amulet is particularly strong against undead. And the amulet of glory remains a
versatile choice for players who want multiple combat bonuses without the health penalty. But overall guys,
regardless of whether the unholy symbol and the glory interaction remains available, the important takeaway is
that the best jewelry now depends much more on your combat style, what you're fighting, and how much survivability
you're willing to sacrifice. So overall guys, let me know what you think of these changes. Again, you know, the way
I look at gear in Dragon Wilds, there is always going to be a piece of gear that
comes out on top. That's just the way it is based off of general stats. Whether you're ascending a piece of gear or it's
a jewelry item, there is always a piece of gear that will be out on top simply based on its basic stats. But overall,
depending on what you're doing, what your play style is, and the main way that you approach situations, some of
these jewelry pieces and some of these gear sets could work a lot better for you. So, let me know what you guys think
overall about these changes, not only with jewelry and rings, but as well as just your general thoughts about the
1.0.1 update. If you guys enjoyed this video, drop a like on it and subscribe to All Things Dragon Walls. We're on the
road to 30,000 subscribers. We would love to have you. And as always guys, stay happy, stay hyped, and have a beautiful
